facts.observation: One upper and one lower short horizontal thick rectangular plate. They are parallel and vertically aligned; the lower plate lies directly below the upper plate.

A tall narrow upright apparatus spans the plates. Two near-vertical sides and a dark interior strip with oblique hatch-like strokes are visible. No intermediate plate, lens, dial, person or external environment is drawn.
At the left of the apparatus a vertical double-ended dimension arrow spans the upper and lower plate levels. A small italic l-shaped distance label sits farther left.

The inner dark upright region includes oblique strokes. Individual stroke count and direction are not reliably separable in this low-resolution monochrome source. Do not manufacture a measured internal ray geometry from those strokes.
There is no horizontal velocity arrow and no later dashed apparatus position in this panel.
At left, one solid upright apparatus with upper and lower horizontal plates and the same tall narrow body/inner strokes as the stationary panel.

Two later upright apparatus outlines to its right. Both use dashed upper and lower plate outlines and dashed vertical sides. The three upper plates share one level and the three lower plates share one level; the apparatus stays upright.
A short solid horizontal arrow above the initial apparatus points right. An italic velocity-like glyph is above it.

A solid diagonal light-path segment starts at the lower plate near the right side of the initial apparatus and runs upward-right to the upper plate near the right side of the middle dashed position. An arrowhead on that segment points upward-right.
From that upper encounter, a solid diagonal continues downward-right to the lower plate near the right side of the rightmost dashed position. Its arrowhead points downward-right.
From the rightmost lower encounter, a short solid ray with an arrowhead continues upward-right beyond the last apparatus. This is a continuation, not a third fully drawn clock position.

The light path reverses its vertical direction at the upper plate and again at the lower plate while advancing right. Its two fully shown legs form an inverted V. The solid initial apparatus is left of the middle dashed apparatus, which is left of the final dashed apparatus. No horizontal distance label, time label, angle mark or measured speed ratio is printed.

global: Two panels are arranged left to right, each with its printed panel label below.
Monochrome ink on white; no color coding, grid, axes, scale, numerical dimensions or title within the source.
Original physical apparatus structure and solid/dashed distinction must survive modernization.
New drawing coordinates may implement these qualitative relationships but must never be described as measured source coordinates.
Interior oblique strokes are recorded as visible shading/trace texture without guessing their precise count or treating them as a third external path.
uncertainties: The source velocity glyph is visually italic and v-like; its mathematical meaning will be resolved from raw prose, not an invented pixel codepoint.
The exact nature of the heavy interior strip will be resolved from raw prose without replacing the visible apparatus structure.
